item.title: Oki Island Sea Salt: Boiled from the Sea of Japan — Guide
item.description: The clean, cold waters around the Oki Islands, far from any mainland pollution, make an excellent base for traditional sea salt. On the islands, small producers draw seawater from the Sea of Japan and reduce it slowly — historically over wood fires — to leave mineral-rich salt crystals with a rounded, less sharply salty flavour than industrial table salt. Some facilities open to visitors, showing the boiling-down process and selling the finished salt, which is prized by cooks and makes an unusual, genuinely local souvenir.
